title: Financial Planning for Buying a House in India: Loans, 24(b), and Down Payments
content:
Purchasing residential real estate is a milestone financial aspiration for Indian families. However, taking on an unsustainable home loan can constrain monthly cash flows and derail other essential goals like retirement and children's education.

1. The 3-20-30-40 Rule for Indian Home Buyers:
- Down Payment: Banks in India finance up to 80% to 85% of property value (under RBI loan-to-value guidelines). Buyers must budget at least 20% in upfront down payment savings, plus an additional 5% to 8% for registration, stamp duty, interior furnishing, and legal verification.
- EMI Affordability: Total monthly Home Loan EMIs should never exceed 35% to 40% of your net monthly take-home salary.
- Emergency Cushion: Never exhaust your emergency fund to pay for the house down payment.

2. Income Tax Benefits on Home Loans (Old Tax Regime):
- Section 24(b): Deduction of up to ₹2,00,000 per financial year against interest paid on home loans for a self-occupied residential property.
- Section 80C: Deduction of up to ₹1,50,000 against the principal repayment portion of the EMI, plus stamp duty and registration fees paid during the year of purchase.

3. Prepayment Strategy:
Because home loan tenures often span 20 to 25 years, the total interest paid can easily exceed the original borrowed principal. Making just one additional EMI payment per year, or increasing your monthly EMI by 5% annually as your salary grows, can reduce a 20-year home loan tenure down to 12 years, saving tens of lakhs of rupees in interest.
